headline: CHEAPER AI NOW
USES YOUR **PC**
cover.hook_pick_reason: Answers what changes for ordinary users: a cheaper model that clicks, types and moves between apps is available now in paid ChatGPT plans (slides 1, 2, 4). It promises no more than that. The number options are accurate but hide the everyday-work payoff.
cover.image_prompt: Cinematic wide shot of a dark modern desk at night, a glowing computer monitor showing abstract floating panels while a soft amber cursor-shaped light moves by itself across the screen, faint streaks of light linking several windows, cool blue shadows. Main subject in the upper half, lower third in deep shadow. No text, no letters, no logos, no people.

slides.title: OpenAI's new model runs a computer
body: OpenAI launched **GPT-6.1 Terra**, a cheaper model for everyday computer work. It can click, type and move between apps. It replaces GPT-5.6 Terra.

slides.title: Half the previous price
body: Terra costs **$1** per million input tokens and **$5** per million output tokens. Tokens are the small chunks of text an AI reads and writes. That is half the price of GPT-5.6 Terra.

slides.title: Better, at a third of the cost
body: In one test, Terra scored **15 points** higher than its predecessor at about **a third** of the cost. These figures come from OpenAI's own tests and were not independently checked.

slides.title: Available now in paid plans
body: Terra is available now to ChatGPT **Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu** users, and in Codex, OpenAI's coding tool.

slides.title: A "Critical" cyber rating
body: Terra reaches the **"Critical"** cybersecurity level under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, its internal risk-rating system. Last month OpenAI cancelled GPT-6.1 Astra after it failed internal safety tests.

facts.text: OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Terra, a cheaper model for everyday computer work that can click, type and move between apps. It replaces GPT-5.6 Terra.

caption:
OpenAI just launched GPT-6.1 Terra, a cheaper model that can run a computer for you.

It clicks, types and moves between apps, and it costs half as much as the model it replaces.

→ $1 input / $5 output per million tokens, half of GPT-5.6 Terra
→ In one test, +15 points at about a third of the cost (OpenAI's own tests)
→ Available now in ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Enterprise, Edu and Codex

What routine computer task would you hand to an AI first?

Source: The Next Web, "OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra, a cheaper model for everyday computer work", Oct 26, 2026.
